title: Mississippian Period
text: During the Mississippian Period, shallow seas covered much of North America. Mississippian fossils are abundant in portions of the Midwest and South and include vast beds of limestone and marble. For example, the domed ceiling of the Jefferson Memorial in Washington, D.C., is made of Indiana limestone that was deposited during the Mississippian Period. This period is sometimes called the “Age of Crinoids” because the fossils of these invertebrates are major components of much Mississippian-age limestone. Also noteworthy in this period is the first appearance of amphibians.
